classification.difficultyReason: Students interpret which location is the starting point and apply the taught reverse-bearing procedure to explicitly stated bearings, including where a north ray is absent.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The bearing of $S$ from $L$ is $285^{\circ}$. Find the bearing of $L$ from $S$.

spec.description: C lower left, S above, L lower right; north rays at S and L. Only the central ray is labelled North.
spec.mathematics: L lies on bearing 105 degrees from S; SL has no supplied length.
spec.answerVisibility: No teacher arcs, added rays, auxiliary angles or results.

answer.worked:
At $L$, the angle on the other side of north is $360^{\circ}-285^{\circ}=\color{#4f9b63}{75^{\circ}}$.

The north lines are parallel, so cointerior angles sum to $180^{\circ}$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }L\text{ from }S&=180^{\circ}-75^{\circ}\\&=105^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Given clockwise 285 degrees at L in purple; remaining 75 degrees at L in green; sought clockwise 105 degrees at S in red.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The bearing of $S$ from $C$ is $76^{\circ}$. Find the bearing of $C$ from $S$.

spec.description: C lower left, S above, L lower right; original north rays at C and S, with North above S.
spec.mathematics: CS has bearing 76 degrees from C; no lengths are given.

answer.worked:
The north lines are parallel. The cointerior angle at $S$ is $180^{\circ}-76^{\circ}=\color{#4f9b63}{104^{\circ}}$.

Using angles at a point:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }C\text{ from }S&=360^{\circ}-104^{\circ}\\&=256^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: 76 degrees at C in purple, 104 degrees at S in green and clockwise 256 degrees at S in red.

children.label: c
children.prompt: The bearing of $L$ from $S$ is $118^{\circ}$. Find the bearing of $S$ from $L$.

spec.description: C lower left, S above, L lower right. Original north rays at C and S; North labels S.
spec.mathematics: SL lies on bearing 118 degrees from S; no lengths are given.
spec.answerVisibility: The coloured north ray at L and teacher angle annotations are omitted.

answer.worked:
Draw a north line at $L$, parallel to the north line at $S$. The cointerior angle at $L$ is $180^{\circ}-118^{\circ}=\color{#4f9b63}{62^{\circ}}$.

Using angles at a point:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }S\text{ from }L&=360^{\circ}-62^{\circ}\\&=298^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Purple 118-degree bearing at S; added red north ray at L; green 62-degree angle and red clockwise 298-degree bearing at L.
